A Dubai business may prepare one set of financial statements for local stakeholders and a separate reporting pack for an overseas parent. An accounting profit figure is meaningful only when the policies, reporting period and consolidation scope are understood.

The term GAAP means generally accepted accounting principles; it does not refer exclusively to one country's rules. This article compares US GAAP with IFRS Accounting Standards. It is a practical starting point for identifying adjustments, rather than a complete conversion manual.

Use the correct source for each framework

The FASB Accounting Standards Codification is the authoritative source of nongovernmental US GAAP, with SEC requirements also relevant to SEC registrants. IFRS Accounting Standards are developed by the International Accounting Standards Board. A broad description such as rules-based versus principles-based is too limited to settle a particular transaction.

For a UAE subsidiary, agree the reporting basis with the parent, auditor and relevant stakeholders before designing the accounts. A parent company's reporting instructions should identify the required framework, materiality, reporting currency and policies. A spreadsheet heading saying GAAP is not sufficiently precise.

Inventory: investigate the costing policy

Under IAS 2, ordinarily interchangeable inventory uses FIFO or weighted-average costing. Specific identification applies to inventory that is not ordinarily interchangeable. US GAAP also accommodates LIFO, so a group using that method cannot assume its inventory figure carries over unchanged into IFRS reporting.

For a trading business, retain the item-level movement report, purchase costs, stock-count results and the chosen costing policy. Review slow-moving and damaged goods as well as quantities. A framework comparison should reconcile both cost and valuation adjustments; matching the physical stock count alone does not establish that the reported inventory values are equivalent.

Leases: both frameworks can create balance-sheet balances

It is outdated to say that US GAAP generally keeps operating leases off the balance sheet. Topic 842 requires recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for both finance and operating leases, subject to the applicable requirements and exceptions. IFRS 16 generally uses a single lessee model, with exemptions including qualifying short-term and low-value leases.

Classification, expense presentation and cash-flow presentation can still differ. Collect signed agreements, payment schedules, renewal options and amendments. A rented clinic, restaurant or office may need a lease assessment even when management has historically recorded only the monthly rent payment.

Development expenditure needs evidence

IAS 38 distinguishes research expenditure from development expenditure. Research costs are expensed; development costs are recognised as an intangible asset only when the specified criteria are satisfied. A management decision to call spending an investment does not establish those criteria.

US GAAP has its own requirements, including specialised guidance for software. Avoid applying a blanket rule to every development project. Maintain project descriptions, approvals, cost records and the evidence supporting the accounting assessment.

Build a reconciliation, not two disconnected ledgers

Illustrative example: a UAE distributor sends a reporting pack to a US parent. Its finance team should start from the reconciled local trial balance, identify the relevant policy differences and record clearly labelled reporting adjustments. Each adjustment should show its calculation, supporting documents, reviewer and effect on opening balances and the current period.

Keep a policy register covering inventory, leases and material development projects. Agree recurring entries with the group finance team and revisit them when contracts or standards change. This produces a clearer reporting trail than altering operational records simply to make two reporting packs display the same profit. PLS can help organise the underlying records and reporting schedules for that review.

sections.heading: The reporting deadline starts with your financial year
paragraphs: IFRS 18 replaces IAS 1 and applies to annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with earlier application permitted. For a business applying full IFRS with a calendar year, the first mandatory annual period is therefore 2027. Establish the entity's reporting framework and year-end before setting the implementation timetable.

The change deserves attention before the first year-end close. Account mappings, reporting templates and the information used in public performance discussions may need review. Treating it as a final formatting exercise can leave finance teams reconstructing information under time pressure.

sections.heading: Understand what the new profit subtotals mean
paragraphs: IFRS 18 introduces defined categories and subtotals in the statement of profit or loss, including operating profit and profit before financing and income taxes. The statement also has income-tax and discontinued-operations categories. Classification needs to follow the standard's requirements; an existing account name is not a sufficient assessment.

The business model matters. Entities must assess whether investing in particular assets or providing financing to customers is a main business activity. A holding or financing business should not simply copy the mapping designed for a trading company. Document the reasoning for material classifications and review it with the reporting adviser.

sections.heading: Review adjusted performance measures carefully
paragraphs: Some subtotals used in public communications may meet the definition of a management-defined performance measure. The assessment considers whether the subtotal communicates management's view of an aspect of the financial performance of the entity as a whole and is neither listed in IFRS 18 nor specifically required by IFRS Accounting Standards.

Do not assume every KPI or every figure called EBITDA qualifies. Inventory the measures actually used, where they are communicated, their calculations and their purpose. Public communications can include management commentary, press releases and investor presentations. IFRS 18's definition excludes oral communications, their written transcripts and social-media posts. The communication and the measure both require assessment.

sections.heading: Make the reporting trail visible
paragraphs: For measures that meet the definition, prepare the required explanations and reconciliation to the most directly comparable IFRS subtotal or total, with the applicable supporting disclosures. Assign an owner to each calculation. A reader should be able to understand which items management adjusted and how the measure relates to the financial statements.

Illustrative example: a Dubai business publishes an adjusted profit figure after excluding a relocation expense. The team should retain the calculation and assess the measure under IFRS 18, rather than assuming the label adjusted makes it acceptable. Consistent definitions and documented explanations also help management understand changes between reporting periods.

sections.heading: Test the ledger and comparative information
paragraphs: Start with a sample trial balance. Map the material income and expense accounts, identify balances containing several types of transaction, and check whether additional detail is needed in the notes. IFRS 18 strengthens the principles for grouping and separating information; moving every unfamiliar item into other expenses is not a useful preparation method.

IFRS 18 requires retrospective application and restated prior-year comparative information. A calendar-year business first applying the standard in 2027 should therefore plan for its 2026 comparative data. Run a draft statement using the proposed format, reconcile it to the existing accounts and record unresolved classification questions before the reporting timetable becomes urgent.

sections.heading: A manageable preparation plan
paragraphs: Begin by confirming scope, reporting dates and responsible people. Then review the chart of accounts, assess material classifications and performance measures, prepare a sample reporting pack and obtain technical review. Keep a decision log so the same transaction receives consistent treatment across business units.

PLS can support the practical accounting work: cleaner account structures, reconciled schedules and reporting information ready for professional review. A structured preparation project gives the finance team time to resolve questions and helps owners understand how familiar performance figures will appear in the new financial statements.

Prepare for IFRS 18 with a practical review of profit-and-loss mapping, management-defined performance measures, reporting systems and comparative information.

Originally published on LinkedIn: 10 February 2026. Reviewed and expanded: 2 November 2026.

Original source: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ahmad-helwani_ifrs-ifrs18-ias1-activity-7426889138857099274-2T7C

The reporting deadline starts with your financial year
IFRS 18 replaces IAS 1 and applies to annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with earlier application permitted. For a business applying full IFRS with a calendar year, the first mandatory annual period is therefore 2027. Establish the entity's reporting framework and year-end before setting the implementation timetable.

The change deserves attention before the first year-end close. Account mappings, reporting templates and the information used in public performance discussions may need review. Treating it as a final formatting exercise can leave finance teams reconstructing information under time pressure.

Understand what the new profit subtotals mean
IFRS 18 introduces defined categories and subtotals in the statement of profit or loss, including operating profit and profit before financing and income taxes. The statement also has income-tax and discontinued-operations categories. Classification needs to follow the standard's requirements; an existing account name is not a sufficient assessment.

The business model matters. Entities must assess whether investing in particular assets or providing financing to customers is a main business activity. A holding or financing business should not simply copy the mapping designed for a trading company. Document the reasoning for material classifications and review it with the reporting adviser.

Review adjusted performance measures carefully
Some subtotals used in public communications may meet the definition of a management-defined performance measure. The assessment considers whether the subtotal communicates management's view of an aspect of the financial performance of the entity as a whole and is neither listed in IFRS 18 nor specifically required by IFRS Accounting Standards.

Do not assume every KPI or every figure called EBITDA qualifies. Inventory the measures actually used, where they are communicated, their calculations and their purpose. Public communications can include management commentary, press releases and investor presentations. IFRS 18's definition excludes oral communications, their written transcripts and social-media posts. The communication and the measure both require assessment.

Make the reporting trail visible
For measures that meet the definition, prepare the required explanations and reconciliation to the most directly comparable IFRS subtotal or total, with the applicable supporting disclosures. Assign an owner to each calculation. A reader should be able to understand which items management adjusted and how the measure relates to the financial statements.

Illustrative example: a Dubai business publishes an adjusted profit figure after excluding a relocation expense. The team should retain the calculation and assess the measure under IFRS 18, rather than assuming the label adjusted makes it acceptable. Consistent definitions and documented explanations also help management understand changes between reporting periods.

Test the ledger and comparative information
Start with a sample trial balance. Map the material income and expense accounts, identify balances containing several types of transaction, and check whether additional detail is needed in the notes. IFRS 18 strengthens the principles for grouping and separating information; moving every unfamiliar item into other expenses is not a useful preparation method.

IFRS 18 requires retrospective application and restated prior-year comparative information. A calendar-year business first applying the standard in 2027 should therefore plan for its 2026 comparative data. Run a draft statement using the proposed format, reconcile it to the existing accounts and record unresolved classification questions before the reporting timetable becomes urgent.

A manageable preparation plan
Begin by confirming scope, reporting dates and responsible people. Then review the chart of accounts, assess material classifications and performance measures, prepare a sample reporting pack and obtain technical review. Keep a decision log so the same transaction receives consistent treatment across business units.

PLS can support the practical accounting work: cleaner account structures, reconciled schedules and reporting information ready for professional review. A structured preparation project gives the finance team time to resolve questions and helps owners understand how familiar performance figures will appear in the new financial statements.

This exercise often reveals the real preparation gap. For example, a service charge may have been posted under general expenses while the underlying calculation is held only in an email. Bringing that calculation into the year-end file makes the position easier to explain and review.

Understand functions, assets and risks

Before selecting a margin or interest rate, identify the economic contribution of each party. Who makes decisions? Who employs the people doing the work? Who owns or uses important assets? Who controls and can financially bear the relevant risks? The answers should reflect actual conduct, rather than labels such as consultant or distributor alone.

For an internal service arrangement, a useful working paper identifies the services, the recipients and the evidence of delivery. Timesheets, deliverables and an explanation of the allocation basis can make the commercial narrative much clearer than a single annual invoice.

Select an appropriate pricing method

Recognised methods include comparable uncontrolled price, resale price, cost plus, transactional net margin and profit split. The appropriate choice depends on the transaction, the functional analysis and the availability of reliable comparable information. A convenient percentage is not, by itself, a pricing method.

Internal transactions with independent customers or suppliers can provide a useful starting point, but differences in volume, credit terms, market, responsibilities or risk must be considered. Where external benchmarking is needed, record the search criteria, the selected comparables and the reasons for any adjustments.

Also identify premises made available by the business and customer-facing activity. Use the applicable treaty and domestic law

Where local advice is needed, send those facts together. This is usually more effective than asking whether remote working is generally allowed.

Keep loan pricing separate from deduction limits

For related-party financing, one question is whether the transaction and interest terms meet the arm’s-length principle. Another is whether the resulting interest expense is deductible under domestic tax rules. A supportable market rate does not, by itself, resolve a statutory deduction restriction.

The UAE has general and specific interest-deduction rules, alongside its transfer pricing requirements. A financing review should therefore retain the agreement, amount and currency, maturity, security, use of funds, borrower information and pricing support, then assess the relevant deduction rules separately. The OECD’s changes do not replace that UAE analysis.

Create an approval process for overseas working

Consider a Dubai business whose employee requests an extended stay abroad for personal reasons. Before approving it, management could document the proposed dates, duties, customer contact, decision-making authority and reporting arrangements. If the role later changes to developing that overseas market, the business should revisit the assessment. articles.title: Family Foundation Tax Transparency: Holding Companies and SPVs
articles.description: A practical review of UAE family foundation tax transparency, underlying holding companies, SPVs, ownership chains and the records needed to support an application.

sections.heading: Start with the whole ownership structure
paragraphs: A family foundation may sit above several companies holding investments or property. Reviewing the foundation alone can therefore leave an important question unanswered: how is each company beneath it treated for UAE Corporate Tax? The FTA’s June 2026 Family Foundations Guide addresses these multi-tier structures. Its practical message is to assess the structure entity by entity, rather than assume that one approval covers every company.

sections.heading: Transparency is conditional
paragraphs: Article 17 of the Corporate Tax Law allows an eligible family foundation to apply for treatment as an Unincorporated Partnership. The conditions concern its beneficiaries, investment or savings purpose, activities and absence of a principal tax-avoidance purpose. It must not conduct an activity that would be a taxable business activity if undertaken directly by the relevant individuals. Additional prescribed conditions also matter.

This is a tax treatment requiring analysis; a DIFC or ADGM foundation registration does not by itself establish eligibility. Tax transparency generally attributes the relevant income, expenditure, assets and liabilities to the beneficiaries. Their own circumstances and the character of that income still need review.

sections.heading: Check every company in the chain
paragraphs: Ministerial Decision No. 261 of 2024 permits a juridical person wholly owned and controlled by a transparent family foundation to apply for transparent treatment, subject to its own conditions. Indirect ownership must run through an uninterrupted chain of entities themselves treated as Unincorporated Partnerships.

The June 2026 guide explains the consequence of an interruption: a non-transparent entity in the chain prevents companies beneath that entity from qualifying through this route. Each entity’s approval and continuing eligibility must therefore be checked. A wholly owned LLC is not automatically transparent simply because its ultimate owner is a family foundation.

sections.heading: A practical review example
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical foundation owning Holding Company A, which owns Property SPV B. The review file should identify the legal owner and controller of each entity, its actual activities, the relevant tax periods and the status of each application. If A has not obtained the necessary transparent treatment, an approval for the foundation should not be treated as evidence that B is also transparent.

Before changing this structure, prepare a simple table showing each proposed transaction and the entity affected. Adding an outside investor, starting a trading activity or selling an intermediate holding company may change the facts on which an earlier assessment was based. Those changes deserve review before implementation, with the conclusion recorded in writing.

sections.heading: Build a file that can be maintained
paragraphs: A useful working file connects the legal documents to the accounting records. Avoid leaving the ownership chart, foundation charter and tax applications in separate folders with no explanation of how they fit together. Assign someone to keep the file current and record the reason for each change.
bullets: Keep dated ownership charts, incorporation documents and evidence of control for every tier.
Describe the assets and actual activities of each entity, using contracts and accounting records.
Retain application submissions, FTA approvals and the effective periods stated in them.
Record beneficiaries and how their relevant entitlements are identified.
Review proposed ownership and activity changes before completing them.

sections.heading: Approval is followed by annual compliance
paragraphs: FTA Decision No. 5 of 2025 requires an approved family foundation or qualifying owned juridical person to submit an annual confirmation within nine months after the relevant tax period. The confirmation addresses whether the conditions continued to be met. The decision also sets application timing and effective-period rules; the application date and approval should be reviewed together.

The most useful next step is a documented review of the complete structure, its activities and its compliance calendar. Dr. Ahmad Helwani can help assess the tax position, identify gaps and coordinate the supporting accounting records.

articles.plsBodyHtml:
Adapted and expanded from Dr. Ahmad Helwani’s original LinkedIn publication. This website edition includes current technical updates and practical examples.

A free-zone licence is the start of the review

A free-zone company should be able to explain what it does, who performs the work and where that work takes place. These facts matter when assessing adequate substance for Qualifying Free Zone Person status. The FTA’s summary of Corporate Tax private clarifications covering issuances up to May 2026 gives useful guidance on common staffing and workspace questions. The FTA published that summary in July 2026.

Adequate substance is one part of a wider assessment. Qualifying income, transfer pricing, relevant documentation and the other statutory conditions must also be considered. Meeting a staffing or office requirement alone does not establish that all income is eligible for the 0% rate.

Connect the resources to each activity

Article 8 of Cabinet Decision No. 100 of 2023 links substance to the level of each activity: core income-generating activities, assets, qualified full-time employees and operating expenditure. The relevant Free Zone or Designated Zone location requirements must be considered. Outsourcing can be permitted, subject to the applicable rules and adequate supervision.

For a practical review, write down the important decisions and functions that generate each revenue stream. Then identify who performs them, where they are performed and which records support that explanation. A general description such as ‘group support’ is less useful than a clear account of the work actually completed.

Three points clarified by the FTA

Related-party visa sponsorship does not automatically prevent an employee from counting. The clarification considers full-time work in a Free Zone under the company’s control and supervision, with the company bearing the economic cost and responsibility for the substance of the employment relationship.

Shared workspace may be sufficient where it supports the company’s actual core activities at the relevant scale. A passive or asset-based activity has no automatic exemption from the substance test. Its resources still need a case-specific assessment.

Turn the explanation into an evidence file

A hypothetical group may have staff sponsored by one entity while another free-zone company receives their services. Rather than relying only on the visa records, the review should follow the day-to-day arrangement: who directs the work, approves leave, evaluates performance, incurs the cost and keeps the work product? Differences between the written arrangement and actual practice should be resolved and documented.

The following working papers make the assessment easier to review. They are practical preparation steps, rather than a promise that the company qualifies.

  • Prepare an activity and revenue map supported by customer contracts and invoices.
  • List the people performing significant functions, their qualifications, location and responsibilities.
  • Keep employment or service arrangements, payroll evidence, cost allocations and relevant approvals.
  • Describe how the workspace and equipment support the actual work.
  • For outsourced functions, retain the agreement, deliverables and evidence of oversight.
  • Reconcile the explanation to the accounting records and investigate unexplained differences.

Check audit and continuing compliance

Where Corporate Tax rules require audited financial statements, the FTA summary confirms that an overseas auditor alone does not satisfy the requirement: the auditor must be registered with the UAE Ministry of Economy and practise in the UAE.

Keep the substance assessment under review when the business hires staff, changes offices, adds a revenue stream or outsources an important function. A short annual review is easier to support when the records have been maintained throughout the year.
